title: 千問辦公2.0釋出，首個支援多人與Agent協作的Team Agent來了
abstract: 千問辦公2.0釋出，首個支援多人與Agent協作的Team Agent來了 量子位的朋友們 2026-11-09 16:34:03 來源： 量子位 11月9日，千問辦公釋出2.0版本 11月9日，千問辦公釋出2.0版本，這是其上線三個月以來最大的一次升級。該版本推出了行業首個支援多人與Agent協作的功能“協作”，同時上線“人機共創”、“資料空間”、“自動任務”和“三端互聯”等核心能力，讓Agent從服務個人走向服務團隊和組織。目前，所有功能已在千問辦公客戶端全量上線。 千問辦公在同日釋出的官方部落格《千問辦公2.0：主動與協同，邁向Team Agent時代》中指出，主流辦公Agent的產品形態仍以服務個人為主，團隊的協作方式並未發生變化，下一代Agent需要進入團隊協作的現場。 千問辦公推出的“協作”功能率先把Agent帶進工作群，使用者可以組建一個團隊和數字員工共同工作的協作空間。真實的工作通常發生在辦公軟體的群裡，一個複雜專案的資訊可能會分散在多個群聊和會議紀要中，成員只能手動搬運、彙總資訊。現在，數字員工在協作空間內能即時關聯多個釘釘群聊、文件、AI表格和AI聽記等資訊源，支援多個會話並行，以及任務管理與指派。成員在協作空間內指派任務，數字員工就能結合空間的上下文，梳理進展、總結共識、建立並跟進待辦。 據介紹，銀泰百貨卡券運營團隊基於該功能大幅提升了團隊工作效率。過去，該團隊5名運營人員要在60多個門店群裡逐一收集卡券提報資訊，核對後再回填到表格。現在，團隊把這些門店群和一張AI表格關聯到同一個協作空間，原有的溝通方式不變，Agent可跨群彙總資訊並自動更新表格，顯著減少了運營團隊的工作量。 千問辦公上線的 “自動任務”功能，首次讓Agent從被動響應，升級為主動幫使用者幹活。千問辦公官方部落格指出，下一代企業級Agent需要具備感知業務、主動推進的能力，而不是等人啟動。基於“自動任務”功能，使用者可以訂閱事件、配置規則，條件滿足時Agent自動開始處理。目前，該功能首批支援指定人的訊息、指定群內@自己的訊息、審批任務等觸發場景。 以線下門店管理場景為例，區域經理要同時關注多家門店，不同門店的缺貨反饋很容易被大量群訊息淹沒。現在，區域經理使用“自動任務”設定觸發條件“群裡有人@我說缺貨，就讀取庫存表，發起調貨申請”後，只要有店員傳送缺貨相關資訊，千問辦公便可結合群聊上下文讀取庫存，並自動將調貨資訊填入表格裡，區域經理無需一直盯群。 千問辦公還推出了“人機共創”能力，實現對話、內容預覽與產物編輯的打通。使用者基於該能力，無需跨軟體查閱、修訂，即可在對話方塊內邊看文件預覽邊提修改要求，也可以直接選中段落、單元格、幻燈片或應用區域，標記多處意見後一次提交，AI根據修改意見在原文件中直接修改。針對線上文件、AI表格、宜搭應用，該功能還可支援多人、多Agent線上同時共創。 新上線的“資料空間”則可收錄AI生成和使用者上傳的圖片、文件、表格、PPT、網頁、應用和本地檔案，並支援檢視、搜尋、分享等操作，選中單一或多份檔案還能直接發起新對話，或通過“人機共創”繼續修改。例如，使用者選中多份行業調研材料，可直接生成一份市場規劃方案。 此外，千問辦公2.0還進一步拓展了使用者的使用場景，支援手機、電腦、網頁三端即時同步任務、對話和產物，任務在雲端執行，電腦關機後任務照常執行。使用者授權後，離開工位也能通過手機遠端操作電腦。 作為業界首個企業級Agent，千問辦公此前已初步打通釘釘、飛書、企業微信等IM軟體。隨著IM軟體、原生Office和SaaS軟體的原子能力整合到Agent客戶端，千問辦公已向企業級Team Agent演進，引領了人機協作的新範式。 本文由千問提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 千問 量子位的朋友們 倒計時一週｜量子位2026人工智慧年度榜單徵集即將截止！ 2026-11-09 香港金融科技周 x StartmeupHK 2026圓滿結束，吸引逾48000與會者 匯聚全球創新力量與增長機遇 2026-11-09 百度文心首次披露RSI進展：ERNIE Evolve已用於最新模型研發，文心5.5 Flash 或將近期釋出 2026-11-09 敘事奔湧，何以為錨?丨第 20 屆中國投資年會·有限合夥人峰會即將啟幕 2026-11-09 相關閱讀

title: 敘事奔湧，何以為錨?丨第 20 屆中國投資年會·有限合夥人峰會即將啟幕
abstract: 敘事奔湧，何以為錨?丨第 20 屆中國投資年會·有限合夥人峰會即將啟幕 量子位的朋友們 2026-11-09 16:26:45 來源： 量子位 釐清故事與現實的邊界，迴歸投資與產業的底層邏輯。 2026年的創投市場，資金在迴流，信心在修復。機構LP出資規模站上萬億臺階，AI與機器人賽道持續吸納著市場上最密集的資金。數字是亮眼的，但亮眼之下，另一種力量正在主導資金的流向：一個關於“中國版SpaceX”的想像，一句“機器人的iPhone時刻”的斷言——這些關於硬科技必然主導的集體信念，正在定義什麼值得下注。羅伯特·席勒曾將這種現象稱為“敘事經濟學”——有感染力的故事像流行病一樣傳播，改變人們的消費、投資與決策。過去半年裡，創投市場以極高的效率驗證了這一理論。 問題不在於敘事本身。好的敘事放大技術價值，凝聚產業信心，為創新連結資本。問題在於，當敘事與產業結果之間的界限日漸模糊，當估值錨從商業基本面滑向套利預期，當“先到先得”取代盡調成為熱門專案的分配規則，每一個身處其中的人都需要停下來問一句：誰在主導敘事?敘事之後，留下的是什麼? 2026年11月19日至20日，第20屆中國投資年會·有限合夥人峰會將在上海舉行。本屆峰會以“敘事時代”為主題，匯聚國有資本、市場化母基金、保險資金與上市公司產業資本，在萬億耐心資本再度集結之際，共同釐清故事與現實的邊界，迴歸投資與產業的底層邏輯。 —— 閉門深談 ——敘事之外，回到基本面 峰會首日下午設定兩場閉門座談，均以“投中十問”為框架，指向當下最需要冷靜審視的兩個命題。 第一場聚焦國有資本的角色演進，主題為“專業與耐心——國有資本與未來產業和未來城市”。當長鑫和長存分別以時代佼佼者的身份成就合肥和武漢兩座城市，產業培育成為城市未來競爭的核心戰場。發揮好國有資本的資本牽引作用對於發展未來產業，成就未來城市，具有決定性作用。國資早已超越“壓艙石”的角色，但當出資節奏與考核週期都在變化，問題也隨之變得具體：國資不僅要出得起長錢，還要具備與之匹配的配置判斷與投後能力；各地方如何以耐心資本錨定未來產業、參與未來城市的長期建設，使命與回報之間的平衡又該如何落地，本場閉門座談將帶來一些對答案的探索。 第二場回到價值本身，主題為“在結構性新週期中，價值資產在哪裡?”。資金高度集中於少數賽道與少數團隊，中間地帶幾近真空。這是理性的選擇，還是敘事裹挾下的擁擠?當共識過於集中，當資金以極高的密度湧向敘事最密集的幾條賽道，價值究竟藏於共識的中心，還是散落在尚未被敘事照亮的邊緣?要知道不遠的歷史上的Home Run案例，基本都誕生於前期的非共識賽道。因為共識過度集中的投資最後基本都會變成“擊鼓傳花”和“數字算計”的遊戲，脫離“風險投資”的初衷。我們這場座談不提供標準答案，但試圖讓分歧浮出水面。 —— 主論壇 ——拆解敘事鏈條上的每一個環節 次日的議程從宏觀到微觀，從資本到產業，逐層展開對“敘事時代”的解剖。 上午議程從週期研判切入，層層剝開當下創投市場的底層邏輯。開場演講立足宏觀和產業維度，系統拆解當下新週期的演進規律；邀請代表性國資機構聚焦耐心資本價值，探討國有資本如何賦能區域發展，繪就地方產業經濟圖譜，成就未來產業和未來城市；面向熱度起伏的硬科技賽道，分享嘉賓將穿透資本濾鏡，理性辨析賽道泡沫與產業真實價值；同時從併購的“敘事經濟學”出發，拆解“新敘事時代”的科創併購方案；並探討S基金如何適配硬科技結構性存量資產時代。上午壓軸的巔峰對話以“敘事時代：創造敘事、賦能敘事、成就敘事”為核心，思辨資本敘事在科創投資中的邊界、作用與落地方式。 下午議程以重磅成果釋出拉開序幕，現場正式釋出投中《2026年國有資本創新發展研究報告》，覆盤國有資本賦能科技創新的實踐經驗與發展趨勢。三場圓桌對話分別圍繞“產投共生，錨定科創長期價值”，交流產業資本與創投雙向賦能的合作範式；圍繞“退出是門技術活：時間、節奏與方式”，在二級市場科創屬性逐漸增強，波動變大的背景下，退出時機和節奏成為影響投資成績的重要因素，同時投資機構對於多元化退出路徑的探索和嘗試也一直沒有停歇；圍繞新時期LP與GP關係的重新定義，探索從單向委託走向協同共創、共建投資“新契約”的轉型方向。 當前國內股權投資市場步入存量調整週期，估值分化、退出承壓、募資結構重構等挑戰持續顯現。本次峰會兼顧趨勢前瞻、國資實踐、交易策略與合作機制革新，引導資本回歸產業本源，以耐心資本持續澆灌硬科技創新，為產業與資本雙向共生搭建高效交流平臺，助力中國科創產業高質量發展。 收官環節將釋出“投中榜2026年度有限合夥人榜單”，榜單覆蓋有限合夥人、引導基金、保險資金與母基金等型別，並設“最受關注”分榜，評價維度包括管理規模、投資總金額、投資基金數量、GP業績表現與專業度及聲譽，評價週期為2025年7月至2026年6月。這份榜單既是對過去一年資本流向的梳理，也為下一階段的配置判斷留下一組可參照的座標。 —— 在敘事中保持清醒 ——在喧囂中迴歸常識 敘事從來不是敵人。沒有關於未來的想像，就沒有投向早期的勇氣。但敘事也不該成為估值的唯一錨點，更不該替代盡調、風控與價格理性。 資金在迴流，FOMO情緒也在熱門賽道中蔓延。這本身是好事。但越是在這樣的時刻，越需要有人追問：那些被敘事推高的估值，有多少能在三到五年後經由技術落地與商業化驗證站立得住?那些湧入同一批專案的資金，有多少是在配置價值，又有多少隻是在購買一張“不錯過”的船票? 第20屆中國投資年會·有限合夥人峰會，不急於給出結論。它要做的是拆開敘事，攤開共識，讓國有資本、市場化母基金、保險資金與產業資本在同一個場域裡，用兩天時間，誠實地面對彼此的分歧，也確認真正的共識。 敘事奔湧，錨由“心”生。定下錨點的，未必是聲量最大的人，但一定是那些在故事最動聽的時候，仍然記得低頭看路的人。 【參會指引】 第20屆中國投資年會·有限合夥人峰會 時間：2026年11月19-20日 地點：中國·上海 本文由投中網提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 投中網 量子位的朋友們 倒計時一週｜量子位2026人工智慧年度榜單徵集即將截止！ 2026-11-09 香港金融科技周 x StartmeupHK 2026圓滿結束，吸引逾48000與會者 匯聚全球創新力量與增長機遇 2026-11-09 百度文心首次披露RSI進展：ERNIE Evolve已用於最新模型研發，文心5.5 Flash 或將近期釋出 2026-11-09 千問辦公2.0釋出，首個支援多人與Agent協作的Team Agent來了 2026-11-09 相關閱讀

title: L3大撤退！賓士寶馬官宣不玩了：還沒L2好用
abstract: L3大撤退！賓士寶馬官宣不玩了：還沒L2好用 傑西卡 2026-11-09 15:02:36 來源： 量子位 最早量產的親自潑冷水 傑西卡 發自 ROBO-車 量子位ROBO | 公眾號 AI4ROBO 賓士親自給L3級自動駕駛潑冷水了。 最早把L3帶上公路的賓士，現在不得不承認，這項技術推出得太早，甚至不如一些L2級輔助駕駛的功能實用。 賓士CTO約爾格·布林策（Jörg Burzer）最新公開反思：“ 行動過早，反而還得費力氣去追尋客戶真正的需求。 ” 賓士也用行動表明了態度。 今年推出的改款 S級 ，直接取消了曾經引以為傲的 Drive Pilot L3自動駕駛系統，轉而押注L2級輔助駕駛。 不僅如此，賓士甚至計劃 直接跳過L3 的後續迭代，把下一階段的研發重心放在 L4級自動駕駛 上。 要知道，賓士可是全球L3量產落地的先行者，曾經把 駕駛員能夠合法“脫眼” 作為重要技術優勢。 明明技術等級更高，車主為什麼反而不願意用了？ 全球L3先行者，主動撤退 最近在接受外媒Road & Track採訪時， 賓士CTO約爾格·布林策 透露了賓士對於自動駕駛路線的態度轉變。 他提到，有時候技術推出得太早，反而會發現還需要重新研究消費者真正想要的是什麼。 其中最大的挑戰是 系統的可用性 。 布林策解釋稱，賓士後來意識到，必須擴大自動駕駛系統的執行設計域（ODD），不僅要支援 更高的行駛速度 ，還要覆蓋 更多真實道路場景 。 具體怎麼實現呢？這位CTO也給出了明確方向—— 與其繼續投入資源改善L3有限的使用場景，不如集中精力 完善L2輔助駕駛，再進一步攻克L4自動駕駛 。 賓士決定接下來將積累的感測器配置、系統設計等方面的經驗，先逐步應用到 L2輔助駕駛系統 中。 說不唏噓是假的……畢竟當年賓士L3有過實打實的領先地位。 早在2021年底， 賓士Drive Pilot 就獲得了德國監管部門批准，成為 全球首批獲得相關認證的量產L3系統之一 。 後來到2023年，賓士也是 首家在美國獲得L3自動駕駛部署批准的車企 ，S級、EQS等旗艦車型上都有搭載Drive Pilot。 相比傳統L2輔助駕駛，Drive Pilot最大的突破在於，在系統正常執行的特定條件下，駕駛員可以把視線合法移開道路，不用再持續監控車輛駕駛，也就是我們常說的 “脫眼” 。 看影片、處理其他事務等等，當時也都是賓士重點宣傳的使用場景。 但這其實也是問題所在—— 雖然能夠合法脫眼，真正允許脫眼的機會卻十分有限。 以美國版Drive Pilot為例，由於監管限制，系統最高執行速度被限制在 64km/h ，而且只能在符合要求的特定道路、交通及環境條件下開啟。 換句話說，這套L3系統主要適用於高速公路擁堵等少量場景。一旦交通恢復正常，車速提升，系統就可能不再滿足執行條件。 儘管賓士也在持續技術升級，到2024年底，Drive Pilot在德國獲得新的監管批准，最高執行速度已經提高到了95km/h，但系統仍然受到道路、環境等執行條件約束。 何況，這套系統的價格也不便宜，Drive Pilot在德國的選裝價格為5950歐元起，摺合人民幣 超過4萬元 。 為實現限定條件下的自動駕駛，車企需要投入更多感測器、冗餘設計、地圖支援和安全驗證，但消費者實際能夠使用這項功能的時間，未必與投入成正比。 對賓士而言，繼續圍繞有限場景升級L3，顯然不再是最有吸引力的選擇。 取而代之的，是名為 MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO 的高階L2輔助駕駛系統。 按照賓士最新公佈的規劃，這套系統可以在駕駛員持續監督下，提供從起點到終點的駕駛輔助，覆蓋高速公路和城區道路，包括自動變道、通過路口、轉彎以及響應交通訊號燈等操作。 在德國市場，該功能計劃在 2027年上半年 開放訂購，符合條件的現有車輛也有機會通過OTA獲得支援；而針對中國複雜路況的定製版本，其實2025年年底就已經上車落地了。 這裡需要注意，賓士所說的這個L2++級輔助駕駛，駕駛員還是必須持續關注道路並承擔駕駛監督責任，不能像L3那樣合法脫眼。 不過另一方面，新系統所追求的卻是更廣泛的使用場景，以及更高的日常使用頻率。 一套能夠讓駕駛員暫時不看路，卻只能偶爾使用；另一套要求駕駛員始終看路，卻能覆蓋更多日常出行。 賓士最終選擇了後者。 至於L4自動駕駛，布林策認為，其量產落地可能要等到 2030年之後 ，而且相關能力也將逐步開放。 這意味著，至少在未來幾年，賓士面向普通消費者的輔助駕駛產品，將會以L2級系統為重點了。 L3的尷尬，寶馬也遇到了 其實，賓士並不是唯一一家對L3失去耐心的車企。 今年3月， 寶馬 也作出了幾乎相同的決定： 取消改款7繫上的Personal Pilot L3自動駕駛系統。 而且寶馬同樣是L3最積極的推動者之一。2024年，這家德國豪華車巨頭把L3帶到旗艦7繫上，允許駕駛員在特定條件下 脫眼、脫手 ，最高執行速度為60km/h。 系統選裝價格也是高達5110歐元，摺合人民幣約4萬元，一度是寶馬展示自動駕駛技術實力的重要配置。 對於撤回L3，寶馬研發負責人約阿希姆·波斯特（Joachim Post）給出的解釋是： “消費者需求不足以讓這項業務實現盈利。” 兩家最早推動L3量產的德國豪華車企，如今不約而同地選擇收縮。背後暴露的，或許是L3正在面臨的一場更深層次的尷尬。 按照自動駕駛分級標準，L2和L3最重要的區別，並不在於車輛能完成多少駕駛動作，而在於 系統與駕駛員之間的責任劃分 。 L2階段，駕駛員必須持續監督車輛；L3階段，系統可以在特定條件下承擔動態駕駛任務，駕駛員得以暫時脫眼，但仍需要在收到接管請求時及時響應。 這意味著車企需要為L3投入 更多感測器、冗餘系統和安全驗證 ，承擔比L2更嚴格的 系統安全責任 。然而這些成本，未必能夠直接轉化成消費者感知得到的體驗優勢。 尤其是隨著城市NOA、高速輔助駕駛等技術逐漸成熟，L2系統能夠覆蓋的道路場景越來越廣泛。 反觀早期L3，花費數萬元，卻可能只能在高速堵車時短暫使用。 體驗上，未必比成熟的L2輔助駕駛領先多少；成本和技術要求上，卻要高出一大截。 更尷尬的是，即便車企跨過了L3這道門檻，距離真正的無人駕駛仍有質的區別。 L4在規定執行範圍內不再依賴人類接管，系統必須具備自行完成駕駛任務、必要時安全處置的能力；而 L3仍然沒有徹底解決人類駕駛員的接管問題。 自動駕駛先驅 Waymo ，其實早年間也在這個問題上栽過跟頭。 2012年，彼時還叫 Google自動駕駛專案 的Waymo，曾測試過一套L3自動駕駛系統，讓員工在高速公路上體驗車輛自動行駛，並要求他們 隨時準備接管 。 然而測試發現， 人類一旦習慣了車輛自主駕駛，就很容易放鬆警惕 ，有人長時間低頭玩手機、轉身尋找後排物品，甚至有人直接在車上睡覺。 Waymo由此意識到，讓人類在自動駕駛和人工接管之間反覆切換，可能本身就是一個 難以可靠解決 的問題。 從自動駕駛的第一性原理出發，真正需要解決的，是讓機器不依賴人類接管也能安全完成駕駛任務，而不是讓人暫時放鬆，再要求其在緊急時刻迅速接手。 由此，Waymo最終放棄了L3這條過渡路線，轉而直接攻克L4無人駕駛。現在回頭看，Waymo十多年前遇到的接管難題，其實已經預示了L3的技術困境。 再看在自動駕駛領域同樣聲名赫赫的 特斯拉 。 馬斯克也沒有把L3作為必須量產的中間階段，而是持續推進兩類產品： 一邊是需要駕駛員持續監督的L2級 FSD（Supervised） ，另一邊則是取消方向盤、踏板，面向L4無人駕駛的 Robotaxi 。 這其實揭示了一個可能容易被忽視的事實： L2、L3、L4雖然按照數字依次排列，但並不意味著自動駕駛技術必須一級一級往上爬。 按照SAE自動駕駛分級標準，不同等級主要描述的是人類駕駛員與自動駕駛系統之間的職責劃分，並不直接代表技術水平的高低。 換句話說，L3並不是從L2走向L4必須經過的一站，而是車企可以自主選擇的一種技術與產品形態。 過去，L3一度成為 豪華車企證明技術領先 的重要標誌，誰率先獲得認證、誰率先允許駕駛員脫眼，都曾是值得大書特書的行業突破。 但技術認證和市場需求，終究是兩回事。汽車行業曾經熱衷的自動駕駛等級競賽，正在受到真實市場需求的重新審視。 只能說，在能夠提供足夠長、足夠穩定的脫眼駕駛時間的前提下，L3依然有實際價值，但將其當作獨立賣點的商業價值，卻不再那麼理所當然。 豪華車企的撤退，或許還不是L3的終局。 但屬於高價、低實用性L3偽需求的“大逃亡”，可能才剛開始。 接下來就看國產車企，誰先撤退了…… 參考連結： title: AI接管一家8萬Star開源公司，寫程式碼、派任務、查Bug全包了
abstract: AI接管一家8萬Star開源公司，寫程式碼、派任務、查Bug全包了 文婷 2026-11-09 13:47:58 來源： 量子位 Worker不夠了主管Agent還能自己招！ 文婷 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI 一位AI主編領著三位AI小編，分別盯緊前沿大模型、開源專案和大廠人事。 我把選題需求往主編Agent Sienna手裡一塞，它轉頭便拆起了活，派人、收稿，彙總一氣呵成。 不到 8分鐘 ，它就給我端來了 6條 新鮮熱辣的AI選題： 不er，我茶都還沒泡開呢，一天的選題工作就這麼哼哧哼哧地跑完了？！ 早在半年前， LobeHub團隊 就開始用自家的AI協作平臺搞研發，讓Agent參與派任務、寫程式碼，甚至排查Bug。 現在，AI已經成了LobeHub團隊研發流程裡的常駐成員。 在FrontierHarness的30道軟體工程任務中，其最佳化後的Agent Harness使用Kimi K3完成了21道，通過率達 70% ，每道成功任務的成本中位數為 1.68美元（約11.21元人民幣） ，超過了Codex和Claude Code。 真沒想到，DeepSeek最近還在探索Super-Agent架構，LobeHub早在5月份就已經把類似的人機協同思路做成了產品，甚至直接開源了！ 如今，LobeHub團隊已經把這套工作方式用進了日常研發，讓Agent自己拆任務、派活、寫程式碼，甚至幫忙審查修改。 GitHub上，LobeHub目前也已經一口氣狂攬 8.44萬Star 。 那麼，LobeHub究竟是怎樣讓Agent們從單打獨鬥走向團隊協作的？默契度如何？它究竟又能把工作推進到哪一步？ AI開發AI，LobeHub開發自己 AI給AI派活，AI給AI審程式碼。 這樣的場景，如今早已成了LobeHub研發團隊的日常。 就拿10月28日提交的一次開發任務來說。 當時，團隊希望給任務工具和命令列介面補上一項新功能，讓Agent能夠在建立任務時，直接指定使用哪個模型。 所以，他們把這活交給了主管Agent Nasa 。 接到需求後，Nasa馬上建立了一個編號為T-1149的任務，並直接把活派給了對應的Coding Agent Dario 。 接到任務後，Dario埋頭便敲起了程式碼。 從實現功能、補充測試到檢查執行結果，一通操作下來，它順利交出了一份正兒八經的Pull Request，編號 #21852 。 △Nasa派活記錄、Dario提交PR 但任務還沒完。 程式碼剛交上去，另一位AI同事就趕來“挑刺”了。 這次出場的是OpenAI的 Codex程式碼審查機器人 。 Codex對著交上來的程式碼一通檢查，很快便挑出了幾個需要處理的問題。 Dario也沒閒著，接到反饋後，它轉頭就去修改程式碼、補測試，最後再把作業交回去。 就這樣，Codex和Dario就活像現實中的開發工程師和程式碼Reviewer一樣，一個負責寫，一個負責揪bug，你來我往，愣是把程式碼打磨了好幾輪。 最終，這份PR終於順利通過了人工審閱併合並進了LobeHub的程式碼庫， 一條真實的AI研發協作鏈就這麼跑通了。 △Codex審查意見、Dario修改記錄、PR合併狀態 更有趣的是，LobeHub的Agent甚至已經不滿足於單兵作戰， 開始主動跨專案找其他AI同事搭把手了。 比如，當Agent-foundry專案需要lobe-ui元件庫增加自定義中性色支援時。 放在以前，肯定少不了兩邊的開發者溝通需求、協調修改，再通知對方更新。 但這次， 兩個專案的Agent直接自己接上了頭。 一個提出需求，另一個完成修改。隨著lobe-ui釋出6.0.1版本，上游專案也收到了升級通知，於是順利接上了新功能。 △跨專案Agent溝通記錄、元件釋出記錄 妙啊，以前得靠人類在兩個專案之間來回傳話，現在Agent自己就把上下游打通了。 而且，LobeHub團隊還真從中嚐到了甜頭。 據LobeHub團隊一位研發成員透露，他已經整整三個月沒有在本地啟動過Dev Server。 按照他的個人體感，採用這套工作方式後，開發效率提升了約 3-5倍 。 挺不戳啊，自己造的AI，反過來幫自己開發產品，甚至還開始協調其他AI同事。 這下，LobeHub算是真的把這套工作方式用起來了，而且還同步省了不少傳話損耗。 那麼問題來了。 把同一套系統交給身為量子位小編的我，又會發生什麼捏？ 哎嘿，我真用LobeHub組了個AI編輯部！ 為了驗證這套AI組隊幹活的本事換個工作場景還靈不靈，我決定從自己最熟悉的科技編輯工作下手，親自拉一支AI編輯團隊，給它們安排兩輪實戰： 第一輪， 讓AI主編帶著小編們找選題，並生成一份完整簡報； 第二輪， 看看剛交上來的成果，能不能直接交給下一棒繼續幹，生成一個動態熱點網頁。 來咯，上班！ 實測一：讓AI當一次量子位主編 首先，我在LobeHub裡組建了一支迷你版量子位編輯部隊伍。 選題主編Sienna 負責統領大局，手下還有三位各有所長的AI小編。 Gemini 4 Argon 負責盯緊大廠人事變動，看看最近又有哪位大佬跳槽了； Claude 化身開源星探，專門挖掘GitHub社群裡的新鮮專案； DeepSeek 則負責前沿衝浪，尋找最近值得報道的大模型動態。 一切準備就緒，開工！！ 我吩咐Sienna從人事變動、新模型釋出和開源新專案三方面，分別為我找出2條值得關注的最新動態； 並特意告訴它： 我們的讀者是一群常年關注AI大模型、具身智慧等前沿科技動態的5G衝浪達人。 大家每天通常會花 5-10分鐘 快速瀏覽行業動向，因此選題要新、準、資訊密度高，能讓懂行讀者迅速看明白髮生了什麼、為什麼值得關注，避免基礎科普、泛泛而談和純宣傳資訊。 請每個方向挑選2條值得量子位報道的動態，共6條。 每條包含候選標題、訊息日期、核心新聞事實、推薦理由，以及可直接開啟的一手來源連結。 任務一發出去，接下來我就沒再插手。 只見Sienna有條不紊地給三位AI小編分派任務，組織大家各自開工。 我則美滋滋地端起了手邊的卡美羅焦糖拿鐵，準備圍觀。 結果咖啡還沒喝上幾口， 不到8分鐘，三位AI小編就帶著新鮮出爐的選題和信源出處，陸陸續續地從四面八方趕回來向主編交差了。 更有意思的是，Sienna還真挺有點主編範兒。 收到選題後，它並沒有直接照單全收，而是逐條檢查質量。 碰上信源模糊、找不到一手報道連結的選題，它還會直接列出一份完整的驗收清單，等我批准後就馬上提醒對應的Agent “注意標準啊，重找！” 。 就這樣，一番忙活下來，我點開工作列一看。 嚯！ 一份包含6條最新AI動態的量子位選題簡報，已經整整齊齊地交上來了： 候選標題、新聞日期、核心事實、推薦理由、信源連結一個沒落。 甚至還附上了三位AI小編各自的任務回執，提醒我哪些細節還需要人工複驗。 而眼瞅著簡報已經交上來了，我又突然冒出個新疑惑，臨時追問了負責大廠人事的Agent一嘴。 Tibo這陣子到底去哪了？咋還不發重置？ 結果它居然沒問我Tibo是誰，而是直接順著之前的人事線索繼續查，很快便把Tibo的調崗時間和公開動向梳理得頭頭是道。 甚至還順手給我支了個節目效果翻倍的寫稿思路。 把Tibo和最近跳槽到Tibo手下的Cat Wu放在一起寫，效果會更好哦！ 好好好，真·貼心啊～ 不僅能自己派活、收稿、稽核，臨時加活它也能接住，甚至還會結合我的小編身份，主動出謀劃策。 這AI編輯們，真有點上道了。（doge） 實測二：剛交完簡報，下一棒網頁已經接上了，甚至還能現場“招人” 收完選題後，我又臨時給Sienna派了個新活。 這次，我希望它可以直接把剛才的選題簡報做成一張能篩選、能搜尋、還能跳轉一手信源的 AI資訊網頁 。 而且不許重新聯網找新的，必須沿用上一輪的選題成果。 本以為Sienna會把原來的三位AI小編，統統叫回來繼續幹活。 結果它自己先琢磨了一番。 人事小編的專長跟網頁開發八竿子打不著啊，乾脆不叫它了。 找大模型和開源專案的Agent雖然有那麼點相關，但用著用著多少也有些專業不對口。 臨時缺人怎麼辦？ 那就現場招！ （簡直驚呆我了，我甚至是任務結束後開啟側邊工作列才發現的…） 摸索了大約10分鐘，Sienna直接原地新建了兩位Worker，一個叫 “量子位簡報網頁開發” ，負責網頁製作； 另一個叫 “量子位網頁獨立QA” ，專門負責質量測試與驗收。 而且， 新來的Worker直接接上了上一輪的6條選題 ，分頭開始完成內容整理、網頁開發和QA驗收。 全程不用我再重新喂一遍素材。 很快， 6條資訊的結構化文案率先交付，4項檢查全部通過。 隨後，網頁開發Worker馬上敲起了程式碼，QA則同步挑出了兩個問題。 開發Worker接到反饋，轉頭便果斷地修改起來。 最終，一個AI資訊熱點看板順利出爐，全程耗時約 30分鐘。 相信我，我是真沒想到啊… Sienna居然已經可以開始根據任務需要，自己調兵遣將了。 更絕的是，它還知道什麼時候該換人，以及怎樣讓新同事接住上一棒的成果。 而我從頭到尾，除了批閱，都沒再餵過一條新指令。 電腦關了，這群Agent為什麼還能接著幹？ 看到這裡，可能有小夥伴要問了。 為什麼Sienna新招來的Worker，居然還能直接接住上一輪的工作？ 關鍵就在於， LobeHub把工作目標、任務進度、交付檔案和驗收記錄放進了一套共享工作空間裡。 主管Agent可以圍繞已有成果安排後續任務，接手的Worker也能夠知道此前已經完成了什麼、接下來需要做什麼。 所以我不用再把6條選題重新喂一遍，新一輪工作就已經接上了。 那麼這群Agent既能自己派活，又能臨時招人，甚至跨專案接力，到底是怎麼做到的呢？ 答案就藏在LobeHub的一套工作機制裡。 首先， Agent的工作不再被聊天框拴住了。 LobeHub把負責持續執行任務的Agent Loop、儲存任務狀態的Session，以及呼叫工具的執行環境拆開管理。 這樣一來，即使使用者退出對話，Agent也不必跟著停工。 只要任務執行在可持續執行的環境中，它就能在後臺繼續推進，並保留之前的工作進度。 LobeHub團隊還曾用一項客戶端資料遷移任務試水： 這群Agent一口氣足足跑了 2天3小時47分鐘 ，期間拆出了 60個 任務，完成 56次 獨立遷移。 兩天不眠不休啊…6，AI牛馬們這回是真能自己埋頭幹活了… △長期Goal執行記錄 光能一直幹還不夠， 不同Agent之間還得能接上活。 為此，LobeHub把工作目標、任務進度和交付成果組織起來，讓接手的Agent知道上一位同事幹了什麼、自己接下來該幹什麼。 於是就出現了前面那一幕： 我剛收完6條選題，第二輪就能拿著現成的簡報做出AI熱點看板網頁。 當然了，活能交出去，質量可不能跟著撒手不管。 LobeHub還配備了 Acceptance多模態驗收能力 。 Agent交作業時，除了最終成果，還會隨之附上測試結果、截圖、錄屏等證據。 所以我們可以直接檢視實際效果，發現問題就直接打回去修改，滿意了再確認通過。 就像我第二輪實測中看到的，網頁程式碼雖然交了上來，但檢查項沒全部通過，就還不能直接算作完成驗收。 這便意味著， 在LobeHub這套工作流裡，儘管Agent一個個幹活飛快，但人類始終牢牢掌握著最終的驗收權。 △Acceptance驗收機制 於是，一套既能讓Agent組隊幹活，又能讓人類掌管驗收權的工作流，就這樣跑通了。 從LobeChat到LobeHub，他們一步步把AI嵌進公司 其實，LobeHub也不是一夜之間就學會了讓AI組隊幹活。 早在2023年，他們就開源了AI聊天工具 LobeChat 。 此後，隨著Agent、工具呼叫、知識庫等能力陸續加入，LobeHub家的AI一步步走出了聊天框。 2026年1月，LobeHub 2.0進一步引入Agent Group、Memory等功能，讓多個Agent開始組隊協作。 到了5月，他們又推出了 CAO（首席智慧體運營官） 相關編排能力，連拆任務、派活、協調其他Agent這些事，也開始交給AI自己張羅。 巧的是， 英雄所見略同 。 這套思路恰好與最近引發熱議的 DeepSeek Super-Agent架構探索 不謀而合。 而LobeHub早在半年前，就已將相關協作能力做成了產品，如今更是將其開源，讓其他開發者也能自行部署體驗。 更有意思的是， 這家公司還先拿自己開刀。 自己造的Agent，反過來參與開發自家的產品，從寫程式碼、審PR到跨專案接力，真正融入了日常研發。 眼瞅著AI同事們越來越能幹，LobeHub還提出了一個更大膽的目標， Self-Driving Organizations（自驅動組織） 。 按照他們提出的L1—L5分級，目前團隊內部已經執行在L3階段，部分場景正在向Agent能夠自主派活、接力、驗收的L4 “自治業務單元” 邁進。 △Self-Driving Organizations 而回頭看我這次的實測，也挺有意思的。 LobeHub用LobeHub開發LobeHub； 我也真的用它開發了一支量子位AI編輯部。 兩種完全不同的工作，最終都跑在了同一套協作邏輯上。 這或許就是AI Native組織下一階段的模樣。 AI負責把活幹好，人負責決定往哪走。 人機各展所長，最終實現1+1＞2的效果。 Anyway， LobeHub已經把這套AI協作平臺的原始碼放上了GitHub，感興趣的小夥伴可以自己部署體驗一下。 也歡迎大家親自上手試試，來評論區跟我們分享，你們的AI同事又整出了什麼新活呀！ （P.S. 悄咪咪地說一聲，其實我寫這篇文章所需要的資料，基本也都是LobeHub幫我整理的哦，嘿嘿。╮(‵▽′)╭） 體驗地址指路： https://lobehub.com/ GitHub指路： https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 文婷 智譜新模型，懂法方面全球第一了 2026-10-17 陶哲軒：數學2.0時代已至！ 2026-10-11 24天！Jev估值翻至75億美元，年度矽谷最爽逆襲了吧 2026-10-10 Nano Banana終於2.1了！4K直出，中文進步太明顯 title: 基元律動釋出NeoHorse-1.5-Flash Preview，Agent模型RSI進入第二輪迭代
abstract: 基元律動釋出NeoHorse-1.5-Flash Preview，Agent模型RSI進入第二輪迭代 量子位的朋友們 2026-11-09 13:09:23 來源： 量子位 11月5日，基元律動（TokenRhythm）釋出Agent原生模型NeoHorse-1.5-Flash Preview。 11月5日，基元律動（TokenRhythm）釋出Agent原生模型NeoHorse-1.5-Flash Preview。該模型基於Qwen3.8-Flash進行訓練，總參數180B、啟用參數6B，重點提升Agent任務執行與軟體工程能力，目前開放限量內測。 據公司公佈的對照評測，相較基座模型，新模型在Agents’ Last Exam上的整體得分提高9.23分，在Natural Language to Repository評測上的整體得分提高5.92分。其中，物理科學任務提升超過20分，開發工具與測試、Web開發、安全認證與加密等方向也有改善。 本次釋出延續了NeoHorse系列對遞迴自我改進（RSI）的探索，基元律動將其稱為這一機制的“第二圈”。9月釋出NeoHorse-1後，公司將上一代模型重新放回模型池，在實際任務中收集執行反饋，再將這些經驗用於後續訓練，模型訓練尺度也從首輪4B、9B擴展至Flash檔位。 這條路徑依託TokenRhythm多模型平臺和開源Agent產品OpenSquilla。路由系統提供任務能力需求訊號，多模型融合則讓多個前沿模型處理同一任務，形成可比較的執行結果。NeoHorse與這些結果之間的差異，被用於識別能力短板、確定訓練方向，並轉化為學習訊號。 在模型釋出翌日，基元律動還更新了OpenSquilla，完善了這一執行基礎。新版根據任務意圖選擇模型檔位，繼續任務時沿用原檔位，重做時逐級升檔；同時支援獨立更新TokenRhythm和OpenRouter推薦方案，使用者無需升級客戶端，即可預覽差異並確認應用。本期推薦配置也依據十一月模型榜單調整，使執行側的模型選擇能夠跟隨評測結果持續更新。 圍繞RSI訓練，團隊提出多模型差分診斷、對抗式環境進化和群體智慧線上學習三項技術，分別對應能力診斷、分佈塌縮和迭代效率。其中，環境進化引擎持續生成並篩選新任務，群體智慧線上學習利用模型輸出與融合結果的差異進行訓練，將執行框架中產生的比較資訊用於後續最佳化。 公開演示呈現了具體任務中的差異。在表格網頁案例中，基座模型生成的部分計算單元格出現公式報錯，新模型則展示了公式輸入、計算結果及更多互動功能。釋出材料還列出了圖表生成、量子物理計算和機器人裝配參數求解等案例，考察模型在計算、檢查和交付環節的完成情況。 NeoHorse-1.5-Flash Preview現可通過基元律動官方公眾號申請內測。 本文由基元律動提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 基元律動 量子位的朋友們 當AI在加速狂奔，什麼反而應該“慢”下來？ 2026-11-09 尋找最會講故事的AI創作者，虎鯨文娛鯨銳AI創作大賽走進清華大學 2026-11-09 終端側AI：從單點應用走向智慧體體驗 2026-11-08 為什麼每個 Personal Agent 背後，都必須配備一臺“雲電腦”？ 2026-11-06 相關閱讀

title: 當AI在加速狂奔，什麼反而應該“慢”下來？
abstract: 當AI在加速狂奔，什麼反而應該“慢”下來？ 量子位的朋友們 2026-11-09 11:47:12 來源： 量子位 “讓人放心，把人放大。” 加速時代的悖論： 當“你的 AI”開始對“我的 AI”說話 2026 年，人工智慧正在經歷一次深刻的角色跨越：從過去幾年的“對話互動”，全面走向“自主交付”。 過去，AI 停留在螢幕側邊欄的對話方塊裡，你問它答，提供的是參考建議；而今天，智慧體（Agent）開始走出對話方塊，真正嵌入日常工作流。作為國內使用者規模最大的 AI 辦公提效智慧體，騰訊 WorkBuddy 在經歷 100 餘次版本迭代後，已累計承接超過 90 億次任務請求，帶動 Token 消耗增長 50 倍以上；據第三方 AI 產品榜 8 月桌面端資料，國內 AI 辦公智慧體桌面端總月活已達 3316 萬，其中 WorkBuddy 位列總榜第一，月活規模佔該賽道三分之一以上。 在企業的業務一線，蒙牛通過內部 AI 創新大賽跑出 45 個“數字員工”，將單牧場診療時效從 1.5 天縮短到 2 小時；上海家化在 9 大部門規模化落地 WorkBuddy，將每月 4.5–6 人天的 6000 萬行物流賬單對賬壓縮到 20 分鐘以內。 單點工作流的提效，已經是不爭的事實。但當我們在 AI 的加速度裡一路狂奔時，一種微妙的職場異化也在悄然發生： 在不少率先普及 AI 工具的機構裡，彙報材料和文件裡的“AI 味”越來越濃。往往是一個人用 AI 在幾分鐘內生成了洋洋灑灑的萬字長文，發給另一端；另一端的同事根本來不及細看，又用自己的 AI 把這篇長文濃縮成三條摘要。 當溝通演變成“你的 AI 對著我的 AI 說話”，資訊的體積膨脹了數倍，人與人之間真實的思想碰撞卻被稀釋了。 這正是 2026 騰訊全球數字生態大會丟擲的那個直擊痛點的追問： 一個充滿“超級個體”的團隊，自動就是“超級團隊”了嗎？ 答案通常並不樂觀：還不是。如果部門之間依然靠漫長的會議去對齊口徑，如果同樣的方案還在不同團隊重複造輪子，如果關鍵經驗依然鎖在少數人腦子裡——那麼，個體的單兵速度越快，製造出的資訊洪流就越容易轉化為組織內部消化與甄別的負擔。單點的效率提上去了，群體的協同卻被摩擦抵消了。 當全行業都在高喊“AI Native（AI 原生）”的時候，或許我們更需要一點“People Native（以人為本）”的清醒。作為一家 AI 科技企業，騰訊始終秉持著一個清晰、有溫度且直擊本質的價值主張： “讓人放心，把人放大。” 在今年的全球數字生態大會上，這一主張被具象化為一套以 “以人為本” 為軸心的 「AI 原生生產力飛輪」 ——以 AI 原生工作流推動效率提升，以 AI 原生技術架構保障可管可控，以 AI 原生組織促進人機協同與創新湧現。在這套飛輪背後，藏著智慧體時代關於“快與慢”、“機器與人”、“個體與共同體”的深層辯證法。 讓人放心： 唯有底層“可管可控”， 技術才能走向組織的“規模應用” 為什麼在企業進化的飛輪裡，當工作流跑起來之後，必須立刻由技術架構接棒實現“高效執行、可管可控”？因為當 AI 從“陪人聊天”轉向“替人辦事”，人與機器的信任邏輯發生了根本改變。 在生成式 AI 剛出現的時候，人們對它的心態像是在看一個蹣跚學步的孩童——它能寫詩、能畫畫，偶爾答非所問，使用者會覺得新鮮，包容度極高。但當工作流中的任務請求以數十億次計爆發，當智慧體真正進入企業的核心業務流、開始替人改程式碼、核賬目、發通知、跑審批時，寬容就會讓位於審慎：它會不會越權看到不該看的隱私？萬一它在後臺跑偏了邏輯，誰來為結果兜底？ 速度改變的是工作方式，但絕不能降低工程與制度的標準；穩定性、安全性與可用性，始終是數字化時代不可讓渡的長期資產。沒有技術架構上的“可管可控”，AI 就永遠只能停留在小範圍的個人嚐鮮，無法邁向企業級的“規模應用”。 在人類社會中，我們之所以敢把一件事交給同伴去辦，不是因為對方永遠不會犯錯，而是因為彼此之間有清晰的分寸、兜底的機制與透明的溝通。騰訊對底層 AI 原生技術架構（Agent Infra）的重構，如果剝開技術的外殼，在人文與治理意義上其實是在確立三重關於“放心”的制度契約： 第一，是懂分寸的許可權邊界——“代人跑腿，但絕不越權”。 人與代理者之間最忌邊界模糊。在騰訊構建的安全體系與企業微信機制中，有一條鐵律：智慧體可以代人執行任務，但絕不預設繼承人的全部許可權。它只以“你”本人的授權視野去辦事——你平時看不到的文件、進不去的群，AI 同樣無法觸碰；而一旦涉及對外發送訊息、修改核心配置等敏感動作，系統必須停下來，等待你本人在客戶端完成二次確認。 第二，是能兜底的容錯空間——“給探索留出餘地，給失誤裝上圍欄”。 無論是人的創新還是智慧體的探索，都離不開試錯。許多機構之所以對規模化引入 AI 望而卻步，是因為在生產系統裡“錯不起”。為此，底層的開源安全沙箱給每個智慧體開闢了獨立的“數字工位”，在計算、網路、資料與憑證上劃定四道剛性圍欄—— “不干預它的靈活性，只管住它不可控的部分。” 同時，環境狀態支援隨時儲存與回退：哪怕智慧體在嘗試中走錯了路，也能退回上一刻換條路徑重來，將試錯的代價嚴格鎖在圍欄之內。 第三，是可追溯的透明過程——“開啟黑盒，讓行動有跡可循”。 未知最容易滋生猜忌。傳統軟體監控只記錄一行報錯日誌，而智慧體“答得不好”往往並不報錯。通過全鏈路可觀測平臺，智慧體在後臺的任務執行、知識召回與工具呼叫軌跡被完整還原。看得見它是如何一步步做出判斷的，查得清偏差究竟出在哪一環，機器才不再是令人不安的暗箱。 說到底，“讓人放心”的本質，是在人機協作中建立起深層的 “人機迴環” ——無論智慧體跑得多快，在關鍵的決策節點上，人始終能看見、能理解、能介入。方向盤和最後的“剎車權”，永遠握在人的手裡。 把個體放大： 從“工具提效”到“本事放大”， 人的自主性與“三個慢下來” 當底層的護欄立住了安全感，個體便獲得了從繁瑣事務中抽身的自由。但隨之而來的是另一個關乎自我價值的追問：如果機器寫得比我快、算得比我準，人的位置究竟在哪裡？ 前段時間，職場輿論場上充斥著各種製造焦慮的討論：有人擔憂“中層坍塌”，有人爭論到底是年輕人憑藉新工具淘汰資深者，還是資深者憑藉經驗壓制年輕人。 但在真實的產業實踐中，我們看到了截然不同的答案：無論過往的經驗、背景與年齡如何，真正的分水嶺從來不是資歷，而是誰擁有 “自主性（Agency）” ——誰懂得用 AI 化的思維方式去重新定義問題、調動資源。 在騰訊“以人為本”的價值座標裡，AI 從來不是為了替代人、矮化人，而是把人的角色從資料的“礦藏”與流程的“齒輪”，重新變回服務的“目的”。這正是此次大會上 「人類職業進化計劃」 所倡導的核心主張： “本事放大，職業進化。” 在 AI 原生工作流中，這種對個體本事的放大體現為一場清晰的人機分工： WorkBuddy 承擔起跨系統操作、整理紀要、核對報表等重複確定的執行工作；而人則退後一步，迴歸思考、創意、挑戰、質疑、驗收與評價。 無論是人力資源、行政、法律、理財投資，還是內容創作、創意設計、高校科研與市場行銷，每個職場人都可以在專屬工作臺上隨時召喚職業領域專家，將行業 Know-how 轉化為手邊的能力模組，並在日常磨合中讓數字助手越來越懂自己的工作習慣。 當“怎麼執行”的門檻被大幅削平、當生成本身變得廉價，人的核心競爭力正在從外部知識的記憶積累，全面轉向內部特質的錘鍊。在 AI 加速生成一切的時代，人恰恰需要在三件事上“慢”下來： 第一，慢下來打磨“品鑑能力（Taste）”。 十份方案、百行程式碼可以瞬間生成，但哪一份方案真正切中要害？哪一種架構真正經得起推敲？AI 抬高了日常產出的基礎水位線，但工作成果的上限，始終取決於人的審美直覺、價值判斷與取捨智慧。能不能做對選擇、把事情真正做好，最終考驗的是人的品鑑能力。 第二，慢下來“用好人腦、說好人話”。 工具越是唾手可得，越要警惕思維的惰性。卸下機械排版的重擔，不是為了讓人交出思考權，而是為了讓人不被眼花繚亂的新概念裹挾，回到第一性原理——去追問一件事到底解決了什麼真問題、創造了什麼真價值。去掉套話與冗餘，把深度思考濃縮在最真誠、最核心的觀點裡。 第三，慢下來建立“高濃度的人際信任”。 智慧體可以替你搜集資料、生成會議紀要，但在真實的社會與商業交往中，人與人之間面對面碰撞出的化學反應、那種在複雜處境中彼此理解與共情的力量，是任何演算法都無法直接生成的。技術越發達，真實的人際溫度反而越珍貴。 把組織放大： 融入既有組織肌理， 在人機協同中增厚資產、激發創新湧現 當個體的本事被放大、底層的安全架構支撐起規模化應用，飛輪便咬合進入了最關鍵的一環：如何從單點的“AI 原生工作流”，真正演進為群體的 “AI 原生組織” ，走出“個人提效、組織內耗”的怪圈？ 過去幾年，不少企業的數字化或 AI 轉型之所以半途而廢，往往是因為陷入了一種推倒重來的激進幻想。但從組織社會學的視角看，任何一家正常運轉的企業，都是由複雜分工、歷史默契與業務慣性構成的有機體。今天還沒有一套放之四海皆準的“AI 時代最優組織架構”， 向 AI 原生組織的演進註定是一個漫長的過程，沒有任何一家企業能夠承受“先把原有的組織架構、業務流程和 IT 系統全部打爛重來”的代價。 因此， 先以開放連線的“AI 原生工作流”無縫融入現有的組織體系與業務流程，不是權宜之計的妥協，而是組織進化最迫切、最客觀的現實起點。 在騰訊長期跟蹤的數智化先鋒企業裡，真正跑通的機構做法高度一致： 不碰組織架構，不改業務流程，不換 IT 系統——從最重複的一環切入，把智慧體放進員工每天最熟悉的入口裡。 這正是騰訊以 WorkBuddy 與 BuddyOne 串聯辦公生態的社會學邏輯：技術應當主動去順應人的習慣與既有關係網，而不是強迫人去遷就陌生的系統。 通過 BuddyOne 構建的“統一賬號、共享記憶、統一管理”新體驗，以及資料平臺對企業微信、第三方 IM 與 ERP、CRM、HR 等系統的連線，改變自然而然地生長在日常肌理之中：是在企業微信裡，WorkBuddy 直接住進通訊錄，成為聊天窗口裡隨時交辦任務的“數字同事”；是在騰訊文件裡，人與 AI 在同一篇文件上即時“人機雙寫”；是在騰訊會議裡，會前預約與會後的錄製、轉寫、智慧紀要自然貫通；也是產品與研發人員走到教育等行業一線，坐到老師身邊，一點點幫他們磨順備課流程、打通系統介面。 當企業微信群聊裡的討論、會議裡的決策、騰訊文件與騰訊樂享、網盤、ima 裡的知識積累在授權範圍內實現“共享記憶”，企業就再也不需要每次都把來龍去脈重新講給 AI 聽。 而當工作流真正長進組織里， “AI 原生組織” 的三重深層演進便水到渠成： 一是促進人機協同，讓每個崗位與行業都有專業搭檔。 從各崗位的託管數字助理（WMA），到醫療、營銷、風控、地圖、智慧座艙等行業專業 Agent，人類在迴路中（HITL）注入語境與審美品鑑，多個智慧體在迴路中（AITL）併網協作抵抗組織熵增，輔助管理者與一線人員做出更科學的決策。 二是增厚組織資產，把個人經驗沉澱為共同體記憶。 通過“評估—培訓—競賽—認證”的全場景服務體系，企業得以系統化地培育內部 AI 人才；在蒙牛、上海家化等通過賽訓結合跑出數十個數字員工的先鋒企業裡，企業進一步將成熟業務邏輯沉澱為可複用技能，配合底層對個人經驗的提煉、去標識與稽核，把某一位先鋒員工摸索出的有效工作流沉澱為整個團隊可直接複用的資產—— “讓一個人做成的事，成為所有人的起點。” 三是激發創新湧現，形成反哺工作流的正向迴圈。 當組織資產越積越厚、呼叫門檻越來越低，最懂業務的普通員工不再只是流程的執行者，而成為新工具、新工作流的創造者。組織內部的“創新湧現”又源源不斷地反哺回業務工作流，推動整個飛輪迴圈增強，最終鍛造出 可交付、可驗證、可持續 的生產力。 以人為本，回到“人”本身 在漫長的任務鏈條中，微小的誤差會隨著步驟累積。這個簡單的數學規律提醒我們： AI 越擅長處理確定性的執行，人類就越要為不確定性的方向與價值負責。 當智慧體走出對話方塊，騰訊在 2026 全球數字生態大會上展示的這套以 “以人為本” 為軸心的 AI 原生生產力飛輪——用高效執行、可管可控的技術架構 “讓人放心” ，用開放連線的工作流與人機協同的組織進化 “把人放大” ——最終指向的，其實是一種極其樸素的迴歸： 不讓溝通變成機器與機器的空轉，而是讓交流回歸人與人的真誠；不讓技術成為懸在頭頂的焦慮，而是讓它成為託舉普通人本事與創造力的底座。 機器的歸機器，人類的歸人類。在 AI 加速狂奔的時代，願我們擁有隨時呼叫智慧的從容，也保有慢下來思考、品鑑與彼此信任的定力。用讓人放心的技術，去迎接那個把人放大的未來。 本文由騰訊提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 title: 尋找最會講故事的AI創作者，虎鯨文娛鯨銳AI創作大賽走進清華大學
abstract: 尋找最會講故事的AI創作者，虎鯨文娛鯨銳AI創作大賽走進清華大學 量子位的朋友們 2026-11-09 10:19:08 來源： 量子位 11月6日，清華大學舉行“新技術激發文化新活力，用AI講好中國故事”鯨銳AI創作大賽大咖對談活動 “好的作品一定要創作者去用心打磨、去主宰內容，而不可能靠AI一鍵生成。拼流量、賭爆款不是真正講故事，希望大家都能做出精品。”11月6日在清華大學舉行的“新技術激發文化新活力，用AI講好中國故事”鯨銳AI創作大賽大咖對談活動上，著名導演、編劇、監製唐季禮談到對當下AI影視創作的看法。 本次活動由虎鯨文娛集團主辦，著名導演、編劇、監製唐季禮，知名作家、自媒體人六神磊磊，清華大學新聞與傳播學院副院長、經濟傳播與發展研究中心主任杭敏教授，虎鯨文娛集團AI劇作工坊總經理張龍，圍繞AI影片創作展開了一場跨越影視、文學、學術、產業等不同視角的對談交流。 “新技術激發文化新活力，用AI講好中國故事”活動現場 保有初心、不博流量，作品才更有魅力 今年9月，虎鯨文娛推出AI人才孵化與培養專案“虎鯨AI人才計劃”，並同步啟動“鯨銳AI創作大賽”，旨在尋找最會講故事的AI創作者，並特別邀請唐季禮擔任賽事評審團首席專家。作為國內首個總獎金池達1000萬元的AI影片創作大賽，鯨銳AI創作大賽共設定265個獲獎名額，單項獎金最高200萬元，面向個人及團隊開放，不限AI創作工具、不限作品題材，作品徵集將在11月22日截止。 投身電影行業四十餘年的唐季禮導演，拍攝過《紅番區》《警察故事3》《神話》等享譽全球的電影佳作。隨著AI技術的快速發展，近兩年他也成為華語電影界最積極擁抱AI的導演之一，並堅持以電影工業標準訓練動作生成模型，其擔任總監製的AI短劇作品《風水天師》累計播放量已經突破13億。“每個階段的技術改革都會改變創作方式，AI會提供很多創作工具，但觀眾永遠關注好故事。要找到跨文化、喚起共情的故事，需要我們下更多功夫。”唐季禮表示。 圖說：著名導演、編劇、監製，“鯨銳AI創作大賽”評審團首席專家唐季禮 面對AI時代的到來，作家六神磊磊選擇的是另一種突破——利用AI技術，從文學創作拓展到影視創作。這位以“重讀中國文學經典”為讀者熟知的作家，近兩年也創作出不少AI短片。當AI把影像表達的門檻降下來，那些他讀了多年、也評了多年的中國經典故事，有了煥發新生機的可能。 “中國經典故事是創作的寶藏，小人物、平視感和共鳴感仍是打動觀眾的重要因素。經典作品的恢宏、多元及其留下的想像空間，也為AI影像創作留下了發揮空間。”六神磊磊認為，市場上對中國經典故事的AI創作改編並不少見，AI工具是先進和銳利的，懷著什麼初心去使用決定了創作出的作品會是什麼樣子，保有人文情懷不博流量，不但是責任感，也讓作品更有魅力。活動現場，他也透露自己正在準備作品參加鯨銳AI創作大賽。 圖說：知名作家、自媒體人六神磊磊 AI創作不僅要有數量、更要追求精品 據DataEye研究院預計，2026年國內AI劇、漫劇市場規模將突破400億元，使用者規模超過6億人；產量上，僅上半年單一平臺新增的AI劇、漫劇就達22.19萬部。而在繁榮的另一面，行業活躍承製方卻從一季度的1216家降至698家。內容行業的競爭焦點，正在從“誰能製造爆款”轉向“誰能持續產出精品內容”。 在杭敏看來，AI內容的精品化轉型迫在眉睫，用AI講好中國故事則成為解題的關鍵密碼之一。這不僅是商業議題，更是文化議題。 “政策、技術和需求紅利給了AI內容前所未有的發展機會，但AI內容數量的繁榮和質量的參差不齊之間依然存在明顯的矛盾”，杭敏表示，AI創作不僅要有作品數量的增長，更要追求精品內容的高峰，“青年既是內容的創作者，也是中國故事的傳播者，希望更多青年人才把握時代機遇，加入到AI內容創作的嘗試當中去，走向國際舞臺，更好地傳播中國文化。” 圖說：清華大學新聞與傳播學院副院長、經濟傳播與發展研究中心主任杭敏教授 創作者加碼精品內容，也需要產業的成熟機制支援。虎鯨文娛集團AI劇作工坊總經理張龍認為，AI創作是技術與藝術的融合產物。AI改變的是創作的執行方式，而不是創作的決策主體；工具的價值在於讓創作者的想像準確落地，而非替代創作者的判斷。要用AI講好故事，技術應當退到創作幕後，和創作者一起定義新一代內容工業的生產標準。 張龍表示：“工具最終的目的是還原創作者的意圖。”他以虎鯨文娛新近上線的行業首個AI影視製作與管理平臺“鯨銳AI”為例分享了業內前沿的技術產品探索。與“一鍵生成”的流水線創作不同，鯨銳AI平臺覆蓋從劇本分鏡拆解、美術資產生成、多模型組合製作到後期調色增強的完整生產鏈路；300餘項精控能力和百人即時協作能力，更切中精品AI內容創作的實際生產需求。 “AI技術帶來創作平權後，對創作團隊的能力要求不降反升。”張龍說，“AI影視創作不是一個人會用模型就能做出不錯的片子，創作團隊的每個人在每個環節和AI精準配合，才能夠完成一次優秀審美意志的整合。” 圖說：虎鯨文娛集團AI劇作工坊總經理張龍 本文由虎鯨文娛提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 虎鯨文娛 量子位的朋友們 title: Databricks' Commitment to European Sovereignty
abstract: Databricks has been building in Europe since our first regional launch in the Netherlands in 2017. Today we serve thousands of European enterprises across 17 European cloud regions. Our growing European team of more than 2,000 employees works from 15 offices in Europe, including several engineering hubs. In addition, European customers can now contract directly with a Databricks European Union (EU) entity, making procurement simpler for customers that require a European counterparty. That investment has always been driven by a specific philosophy: customers should control where their data lives, how it's protected, and who can access it. Our platform is built so customers decide where their data is stored, and who holds the keys that protect it. Databricks is the engine that processes data, not a vault that holds it. Combined with open formats and a multi-cloud architecture, this means sovereignty never has to come at the cost of lock-in. We are extending our partnership by committing to build three new regions in Europe, Azure Italy, Azure Spain and AWS European Sovereign Cloud (AWS ESC). Meeting strict compliance and residency requirements isn’t new territory for us. Databricks was an early leader in GDPR readiness and among the first to build functionality such as “right-to-be-forgotten” deletion management. We’ve continued to evolve our platform alongside regulations and customer expectations, including support for the EU Data Boundary, so customer data is stored and processed where customers choose. For highly regulated workloads, Databricks already operates under some of the world’s most rigorous frameworks . Today, we’re seeing growing interest from European customers in stronger sovereignty controls. To help them continue innovating on Databricks while their data and production environments remain under European control, we’re expanding our sovereign cloud commitments across both Azure and AWS. Microsoft Sovereign Public Cloud brings sovereignty controls to the Azure regions. Databricks and Microsoft are working together to extend those controls to Azure Databricks, including operational oversight, personnel controls, and transparency measures designed to meet the expectations of European regulators and customers. Databricks is classified as a regional service on Azure and has been Azure EU Data Boundary compliant since EUDB launched. We're committing to making Databricks natively available on the AWS European Sovereign Cloud . AWS ESC is a physically and logically independent cloud, operated within the EU, that AWS brought to general availability in early 2026. It's designed to give European organizations the highest levels of operational autonomy, resilience, and data protection, and it's a natural home for the most demanding sovereignty workloads. Bringing Databricks to AWS ESC means customers won't have to choose between sovereignty and a modern data and AI platform. True digital sovereignty is a journey, not a switch. Our immediate focus is bringing Databricks to the Microsoft Sovereign Public Cloud regions and AWS European Sovereign Cloud, and we’ll keep adding controls that strengthen our sovereign offering over time, including support for any open standard compatible storage so customers can keep data on-premises or in European clouds. As the sovereign landscape evolves, we’ll keep listening to our customers and partners and evaluating additional sovereign options based on what they need. Our commitment stays the same: customers should control where their data lives, how it’s protected, and who can access it. Forward-looking statement: This post describes plans and timelines that are subject to change and do not represent a commitment to deliver any specific functionality by a specific date. title: Accelerate GPU training on Unity Catalog tables with UCDataset
abstract: GPUs are usually the most expensive part of any training run, and most teams can't keep them busy. The bottleneck usually isn't the model. It's getting data from where it lives to the GPU fast enough - and every second those chips sit waiting, you're burning both time and money. Today we're releasing the Unity Catalog Dataset (UCDataset) in Beta on AI Runtime. UCDataset is a native PyTorch data loader that streams Unity Catalog tables directly to every GPU in your training job, with no exports, no copies, and no custom loader code. On simulated production workloads, UCDataset cut training time by 10x compared with reading an exported Parquet copy of the same data. Most training data for your models already lives in Unity Catalog tables. Getting it into a distributed training job means picking one of three workarounds, and each one costs you time and money: Then there's the loader itself. Every GPU and every worker needs its own balanced slice of the data. Teams spend time building this by hand, and a subtle bug can mean the model trains on duplicated or skipped rows without anyone noticing. The result: expensive GPUs sit idle, training takes longer than it should, and ML engineers maintain data plumbing instead of improving models. UCDataset makes Unity Catalog tables a first-class data source for distributed PyTorch training. You describe what to read (a table, the columns you need, and a row filter) and UCDataset streams training-ready batches to every GPU. Benefits include: We benchmarked UCDataset on a simulated production workload, streaming a 300 GB feature table across 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs to train a recommendation model and saw on average a 10x improvement in training time compared to loading data directly from Parquet. Say a team keeps user and item features with a click label stored in a main.recsys.ctr_features table. New impressions land on the table every day. They want to train a click-through-rate model on 16 GPUs across two nodes, straight from the table. 1. Describe what to read and create the loader. In train.py, pick the table, keep the labeled training rows, and select only the columns the model needs. The filter is applied as the table's files are read, so rows that don't match never reach your training code. UCDataset already yields whole batches, so wrap it in a standard PyTorch DataLoader with batch_size=None. 2. Train and launch on two nodes. Train with a standard PyTorch DDP loop. UCDataset gives each of the 16 GPUs its own share of the matching rows, so there's no sampler or sharding code to write. Describe the job in workload.yaml, which starts train.py with torchrun on every node, and run it with the AI Runtime CLI: To train on more GPUs, change num_accelerators in workload.yaml. The training code stays the same. The complete train.py and workload.yaml, with a sample table to try them on, are in the AI Runtime cookbook: Click-through-rate model on a Unity Catalog table . Install the package from PyPI. In a notebook, run %pip install databricks-uc-dataset . UCDataset is available in Beta on AI Runtime. To try it: For unstructured data stored in Unity Catalog volumes, use UCVolumeDataset to stream files with local caching. While UCDataset handles structured tables, we are also expanding it to support multimodal training via the FILE type - allowing you to train on images, audio, and documents directly from a table. The Beta reads Delta tables in Unity Catalog. UCDataset (Unity Catalog Dataset) is a native data loader that streams Unity Catalog tables directly to the GPUs in a training job. It's available in Beta on Databricks AI Runtime. You choose a table, the columns you need, and UCDataset delivers training-ready batches with no export step or custom loader code. UCDataset keeps GPUs busy by reading a table's data files directly from cloud storage, without an exported copy in between. It splits the matching rows evenly across every GPU and data loader worker, so each GPU reads only its own share. No. UCDataset reads the live table in Unity Catalog, so there's no export step and no second copy to store or keep in sync. It applies your filter and the table's deletion vectors as it reads, and each new run picks up rows appended since the last one. Yes. On AI Runtime, training jobs read data as the identity that runs them, and Unity Catalog permissions on the table apply. Because the job reads the governed table directly, there's no exported copy to secure separately. In the Beta, UCDataset can't read tables that have row filters or column masks. UCDataset reads Delta tables registered in Unity Catalog, including tables with deletion vectors. title: Turn buying signals into pipeline with Sendoso gifts in Genie One
abstract: AI agents are only as useful as the actions they can take. Genie One lets business teams ask questions of governed data in plain language. The next step is acting on the answer in a way that's governed and measurable, without exporting a list or logging in to another tool. Partner MCP servers in Databricks Marketplace close that gap, and Sendoso's is a worked example: a Databricks admin connects it once, and every Sendoso tool becomes available where your data already lives. Sendoso is a gifting and direct mail platform with tens of thousands of gift options, eGifts, branded kits, custom swag and physical gifts. Its AI suggests gifts, researches recipients and drafts notes, and its MCP server brings that into Genie One, next to the data that shows who to send to and why. Gifting is worth the effort because other channels are crowded: Sendoso's 2026 Digital Fatigue Report found 84% of buyers are fatigued by cold calls and 83% by marketing emails. The signals that show who deserves a gift often live in Databricks already. Acting on them meant exporting a list, logging in to a separate tool and rebuilding context by hand. By the time the gift went out, the buyer had often moved on, and connecting it to outcomes meant manual spreadsheet work. Try it yourself: get the Sendoso MCP server on Databricks Marketplace → Here's what happens in the video (the account and data are illustrative): 1. Find the moment in your own data: The user asks Genie One which target accounts spiked in intent this week and have no gift history. Genie One answers from an intent table in the workspace. The top result is Northwest Robotics, a sample account: intent on gifting automation is up 3x, and the VP of Revenue Operations has viewed the pricing page three times. 2. Turn the signal into a personal gift: The user asks Sendoso to act on it. Genie One brings in the account context from Databricks, and Sendoso searches its gift catalog for something that fits. It proposes a gift and a note built from the reason the account spiked. 3. Preview, then approve: Nothing is charged at this stage. The user reviews the gift, the recipient and the note, and approves it. 4. Track it, or cancel before it ships: After the send, the user gets a confirmation showing what was sent, what the note said, and a send ID. The send ID tracks the gift in Sendoso, and the gift can be canceled until it ships. 5. Show leadership what the gifts did. Gift send history sits in a table in the same workspace, so the user can ask Genie One to summarize the sends for executives. Because the signal, the send, and the send history sit in the same governed workspace: Samsara , Procore and Talkdesk have already shown what targeted gifting can do. In Genie One, teams can run those plays on their own intent data and measure the outcomes they influence. Business users don't need to configure anything. A Databricks admin connects it once: For requirements and step-by-step configuration, see the full setup guide: Using Sendoso in Databricks Genie One → For more plays, see Sendoso's companion post . How do I measure the ROI of gifting with Sendoso and Databricks? With send history in the same workspace as pipeline, renewal and engagement data, you can apply your team's attribution model to measure the meetings, pipeline and renewals gifts influenced, and compare that with what you spent. Ask Genie One for the results in plain language. What is an MCP server in Databricks, and what does Sendoso's do? An MCP server exposes an external system's tools to agents. In Databricks it's installed as a governed MCP Service in Unity Catalog, and Unity Gateway controls which tools agents can call. Sendoso's MCP server makes its gifting tools available inside Genie One, so users can find a gift, send it, track it and see what it influenced without leaving Databricks. Who is this for? Any team that sends gifts or direct mail: sales, customer success, RevOps, demand gen, field marketing, and customer or partner marketing. Users work in plain language in Genie One, with no code. Can an agent do more than the user who is using it? No. Every tool runs as the signed-in Sendoso user, so it only sees what that user can see and only does what their role allows. Unity Gateway policies can restrict it further. Is anything charged before I approve a gift? No. Sendoso first shows a preview of the gift, the recipient and the note. Nothing is charged until the user approves it, and Sendoso's budgets and campaign approvals apply just as they do in the Sendoso app. Can I track or cancel a gift after it is sent? Yes. After a send, you receive a confirmation that includes a send ID, which you can use to track the gift in your Sendoso instance. You can cancel the gift up until it ships. How do I set it up? A Databricks admin installs the Sendoso MCP server from Databricks Marketplace as a governed MCP Service in Unity Catalog and scopes what agents can call through Unity Gateway. Users then add the connector directly in Genie One. Get the Sendoso MCP server on Databricks Marketplace → Subscribe to our blog and get the latest posts delivered to your inbox.

title: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
abstract: Claude Code is leaking sensitive information on public GitHub instances thanks to a partial oversight in the way its settings files are handled. That's the finding of AI security researchers at Apiiro, who discovered thousands of secrets , including database passwords, API tokens, and root logins, amid Claude Code settings files embedded in GitHub repositories. The leak stems from the way Claude Code handles user approval for automated shell commands. When a user chooses the "Yes, and don't ask again" option to approve running a command, that choice gets stored as part of a rule in the local ".claude/settings.local.json" file on the user's computer. That rule is sometimes coded as a pattern, but the command itself is often written to that settings file as is, including any sensitive information that may be embedded within it. This isn't really a significant security issue if the settings file stays on the user's local machine (assuming that machine doesn't become compromised itself, of course). And Anthropic notes in its Claude Code documentation that this particular settings file gets added to the developer's global .gitignore list , which usually prevents it from being shared publicly.

title: Nvidia CEO's affair becomes a national security problem
abstract: Nvidia’s chief executive Jensen Huang has admitted having an affair two days after the FT reported his alleged romantic relationship with a woman the US intelligence community believes was working as a spy for China. Huang revealed the affair in an internal message to employees on Sunday that was obtained by the FT. “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang said in the message. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” In a separate statement, Nvidia said its board would open an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” Huang said he would fully cooperate. “My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust,” he said. “I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to Nvidia and will work to earn back your confidence.” The FT reported on Friday that the US believed Huang had a romantic relationship with a Chinese woman who was recruited to spy for China’s Ministry of State Security intelligence agency. American officials this year wrote a memo, based on information from US intelligence, which said the Nvidia boss had been romantically involved with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of the chipmaker, according to people familiar with the document. The affair is a damaging blow to the Nvidia chief, who in recent years has become the face of the AI boom, one of the technology’s loudest champions, and transformed the Silicon Valley group into the first $5 trillion company.

title: AI R&D Is Accelerating Towards Potential RSI in 2027
abstract: METR came out with an extensive report on how much AI is accelerating AI R&D at Anthropic, and thus how close we might be to recursive self-improvement (RSI) and how far that might go. This is one of the most important questions in the world. Their answer: Things are already accelerating on the order of a 2x speedup. This is several months ahead of the AI 2027 timeline. A naive extrapolation says we may be less than a year away from full RSI. There are no clear bottlenecks in the way. This report updated many towards shorter timelines. This is consistent with what OpenAI and Anthropic themselves have been saying, and with extrapolation from the progress we are observing. We are running out of time. That doesn’t have to be the way this plays out. We could stop the labs. The labs could choose to stop. Or the estimates could be wrong, or some bottlenecks could be hit, or the results could be less impactful than we expect. Indeed do many things come to pass. And if it does happen this quickly, one would expect it to go quite poorly, and likely to cause everyone to die, but perhaps it goes well. METR : These conclusions are based on key empirical findings from the full report. Some of the key findings that most informed our conclusions about risk were redacted. ​ Ajeya Cotra (METR): For the last few months, some of my colleagues at METR have been working on a deep-access investigation to understand how much Anthropic is being accelerated by its AI systems. From my reading of their report and Anthropic’s RSP, it looks like the “dramatic acceleration” threshold has already been crossed. I do not find either of these results surprising. I made minor updates towards faster outcomes and fewer bottlenecks, but not major ones. I had already made major ones. The situation looks rather grim. But this is not a surprise. The information from inside the labs makes you think the situation is grim and timelines are short, but those with that information were already shouting from the rooftops that their secret information meant the situation is grim and timelines were short. Why did you not think this was the standard reaction to their information? I did find it surprising that so many found this surprising, including METR. Their team did not expect substantial acceleration. Ryan Greenblatt expected only 1.15x-1.3x speedup this year . Six weeks ago in the Opus 5.5 system card the estimate was at least a 1.5x speedup . If you are making major updates in response to this report, that is probably good and wise, but indicates you had previously made a mistake in your estimations. If you only look at public models, you can make a case that there is a step change at Mythos but that otherwise the rate of progress has not changed. I was always skeptical of that, but it was a valid claim. Add in the orange data points from internal models and you cannot tell that story. When we include the recent additional internal releases, this takes the estimate from the ~1.7x in the Haiku system card up to a new estimate of ~1.9x. Peter Wildeford : It seems important to realize that: – AI companies have unreleased internal models that are more powerful than the public ones we plebs have access to – Only when you account for these internal models, you can see that AI progress is actually accelerating faster than before – AI companies use their AIs with like 10,000x more compute than us plebs, so they can do much more than we can even with the same AIs You could also have gotten to a similar result by extrapolating the automation graph: Benjamin Todd : Extrapolating Anthropic’s internal AI R&D data results in Claude leading internal research by mid-2027, and plausibly near full automation by the end of 2027, lining up with other methods. (h/t @luc_feron ) The information METR is relying on most is largely redacted. The public report centers on AECI and other estimates. METR is implying that such arguments are merely the legible case they are allowed to make, and that there is a stronger case. Kudos to Anthropic for allowing this investigation. METR : Anthropic offered unprecedented access to internal data on their AI R&D process, including a variety of metrics on pretraining, reinforcement learning (RL), training compute in each domain, benchmark scores for internal models, AI speedup analyses, forecasts of a future model’s metrics, and interviews with relevant staff. This is all highly sensitive stuff, so there are important redactions involved. I would have liked to see less of this, but if this is what it takes to get the report then so be it. I would also suggest to Congress that they should want to see the full report along with everything else Anthropic and Dario Amodei know and really think about this, and to do that they should follow Kelsey Piper’s suggestion and subpoena Anthropic . This is how they describe their subjective conclusions. METR : In our first section, we share our subjective conclusions about risk . We now believe that: Here are their top empirical findings: The goal of the report was to measure acceleration of Anthropic’s internal growth rate, how much of that acceleration is due to AI R&D and whether there exist any important bottlenecks to further acceleration. This requires a lot of sensitive data, and they got most of what they requested. A detailed description of the data we had access to was redacted. A summarized version is as follows: In a small number of cases, Anthropic did not provide relevant information when they deemed it too sensitive.​ Anthropic also offered extensive staff time and expertise to this project. We believe the two staff we worked most closely with are the two highest-context researchers on AI R&D acceleration measurement at Anthropic. Both of these staff met with us frequently for live discussion, and spent substantial time collecting data, doing analysis, and providing feedback. In exchange, Anthropic could redact anything in the report. They did so, aggressively. METR’s only recourse is that it can then share its level of access, that things had been redacted, and whether findings depend on redacted information . Which they do. The majority of the most informative evidence is redacted. METR : We submitted a ~100-page full report on our assessment to Anthropic. For the public version, Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence we found most informative. As a consequence, the public must rely on our judgment more than we consider ideal. Some of these redactions seem clearly appropriate. Others seem questionable. METR : While we were able to freely share our highest-level conclusions about risk, Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence we found most informative for these conclusions. Anthropic described the redactions as “aimed at removing confidential information that could accelerate other AI developers.” Some of these redactions are themselves challenging to describe clearly without revealing sensitive information we have been asked to redact. We share a table of important evidence we were and were not able to discuss given the redactions in our process section below. All redactions that were important for our conclusions are covered by our descriptions in that table or other in-line descriptions in the report below. Much of the redacted evidence we viewed had multiple plausible interpretations, and both METR and Anthropic researchers have significant uncertainty about how to synthesize the evidence into a holistic picture. This makes it hard for the public to judge this evidence themselves, reconcile it with evidence from other sources, and come to their own conclusions (i.e. this report does not achieve ‘transparency about evidence’ ). As a consequence, the public has to rely on METR’s judgment much more than would be ideal, given the weight of the questions answered here.

title: Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude
abstract: Our house has a box room, full of boxes that we still haven’t unpacked from our last move. A couple of weeks ago something in that room started intermittently beeping . The beeps were far enough apart that standing in the room and trying to determine the source of the noise was frustrating, and I really didn’t want to dig through every one of those boxes. So I had Claude Code build Beep Locator , a software system for triangulating the source of a mysterious beep using multiple devices scattered around the room. Here’s what Beep Locator looks like after it has been running for a while: You run Python web server to show the primary UI, and then use the QR code or URL to connect as many devices as you can spare to act as listeners—I was using two iPads, a phone, a MacBook Pro and a Surface Ultra. The devices then play noises to each other to help estimate their locations. This didn’t work particularly well, so I added a “Rough mode” where you can drag their icons around in the space to provide rough locations which are then adjusted based on those sounds. Once that’s set up, the devices all listen for the beep! I added a clapping mode too so I could test it by clapping my hands in different locations around the room—displayed as diamonds on the map. This helped me gain confidence that it was capable of locating a sound. Beeps show up on the map as an X, plus a line in the “Sounds located” log. You can replay these sounds (from each device in turn) to confirm they are the mysterious beep you are looking for, then click “This is the mystery beep” to mark them as such. Once you’ve confirmed the mysterious beep frequency the system will listen out for it, measure the interval between beeps, and use the triangulated locations to lock down the most likely location on the map. The system worked as intended. It gave me the position of the beep to within about 40cm, then I dug through that specific pile of boxes and found an ancient carbon monoxide detector that desperately wanted its batteries replaced. When I started working through this problem with Claude it quickly dug up BeepBeep: A High-Accuracy Acoustic-Based System for Ranging and Localization Using COTS Devices , a 2007 paper by Chunyi Peng, Guobin Shen, Yongguang Zhang, Yanlin Li, and Kun Tan. Here’s that paper’s abstract: We present the design, implementation, and evaluation of BeepBeep, a high-accuracy acoustic-based ranging system. It operates in a spontaneous, ad-hoc, and device-to-device context without leveraging any pre-planned infrastructure. It is a pure software-based solution and uses only the most basic set of commodity hardware – a speaker, a microphone, and some form of device-to-device communication – so that it is readily applicable to many low-cost sensor platforms and to most commercial-off-the-shelf mobile devices like cell phones and PDAs. It achieves high accuracy through a combination of three techniques: two-way sensing, self-recording, and sample counting. That sounded exactly like what we needed to build! Beep Locator runs a Python web application server that does most of the work. The listening devices then connect to that server via WebSockets and present a UI which requests browser microphone access. The listeners mainly work by recording a 60 second buffer of recent audio. They also run a simple beep detection algorithm (see detector.js ), which uses Fast Fourier Transform and a high-pass filter to identify potential beeps. It sends these events to the main server. When a beep is reported, the server has a device play a short chirp (the device with the lowest round-trip time to the server), then asks every listener upload a clip from about 0.6s before the beep to 0.8s after that chirp. This chirp allows the clips to be aligned with each other, a crucial step in locating the beep. I started this project using Claude Code Cloud via my iPhone, with Opus 5.5 running in Extra thinking effort mode. Here’s that shared starter session , which began with this prompt against a newly created empty GitHub repository: Write out a problem.md file describing the problem we want to solve There is a device beeping in a room and I cannot find it I want to set up several devices - laptops, phones, iPads - around the room all listening at the same time and have them help triangulate where the beep comes from There needs to be a Python web app which coordinates it all - one device shows a web page for the app, other devices join a URL which turns them into listeners - all via browser WebAudio and WebSockets back to the Python server app Ideally I wouldn't need to manually input the relative locations of the devices - it would be amazing if they could play sounds to each other in order to locate each other in 2D space - is that even possible though? That got me this problem.md file . As part of writing that up Claude found and read the BeepBeep paper, which is described in that file. The research looked good, so I told it: Ok try and build it, add a mechanism so you can send new code to the listeners which they will then run automatically - that way I can set everything up in the room and then leave you alone to continue hacking and experiment while I do something else That got me to this point —most of the system was built, but nothing had actually tried running it yet. I cloned the new repository to my laptop and fired up Claude Code... and then Fable 5.2 was released , and this project seemed like an excellent opportunity to put that through its paces. I had Claude Code on my laptop start the server running, then made sure it could both see what was happening and make live changes to the software as it ran. This was already baked into the software: Opus 5.5 had built an installModule() method on the listeners that could be triggered over the WebSocket connection, meaning the admin server could execute arbitrary new code on any of its clients. On some devices, web pages that listen on the microphone request user permission any time the page reloads. The hot-swap module mechanism meant that we could deploy new code without having to manually interact with each of the listening devices in turn. From that point on my involvement was mainly to sit by the laptop chatting with Fable 5.2 about what was going on, and occasionally requesting new features. Here are some of the feature prompts I ran: I think we need to make it so I can drag things around on the map in “rough mode”, where my job is just to put them roughly where they are, then switch out of rough mode and it attempts to get them accurate This gave me the ability to drag listeners around the map. what’s a good way for me to test this I wonder? Can we have it listen for claps, then I could clap and it could identify the location of the clap? [...] Claps should use a different symbol on the map than beeps That added the thing where any time I clapped it would show on the map as a different symbol from the beeps. each symbol on the map should include a HH:MM:SS timestamp That made it easier to spot which symbol likely reflected which real-world sound. The log should show beeps and claps with their timestamps AND have a little play button which, when clicked, replays the recorded noise from each of the listeners in sequence (with clear text on screen showing which listener recorded which snippet) while temporarily turning off microphone recording while that replay plays Now I could replay sounds, making it much easier to identify which recorded clip was the mysterious beep I was looking for.

title: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind <details><summary>
abstract: Most of the changes I make to my projects these days come in the form of PRs opened for me by Claude Code or Codex. The PR is my unit of work—I use them to bundle commits together, iterating on them until a feature is complete, document decisions and then merge the finished result. Today’s coding agents are great at writing PR descriptions. The problem is that they are too good. An agent-written PR description is accurate and comprehensive. It describes the problem, the detailed solution, and the steps taken to verify it. That’s a lot of information to absorb. It’s not necessarily slop, but it reads like slop! It’s very easy to spot an AI-written PR, and as with other forms of AI writing my instant reaction is best summarized as “I’m not reading all of that”. It doesn’t matter how accurate or useful the information is, I’m instantly put off by the thought that it will take me longer to read than it took the driving author to write... even when that driving author is me! I want human editorial judgement. I want someone to have thought just long enough about the PR to give me a human-approved introduction that helps me understand, at a high level, what the PR is for and whether it deserves more of my attention. I think I’ve found a low-effort way to do this that feels right. The HTML <details><summary> elements render as a collapsed heading (the summary) that can be expanded to view the larger piece of text. The code looks like this: When rendered, it looks like this : Crucially, <details><summary> is supported in GitHub Markdown . You can drop those tags directly into an issue comment or PR description and GitHub will hide the details and display just the summary plus an expansion arrow. I’ve started using this for my AI-generated pull requests. The opening paragraph of my PRs will be carefully selected to act as a high-level explanation of what’s going on—the shortest text a human can read that will help get them up to speed. I’ll sometimes throw in a screenshot as well, since images are often the best way to quickly illustrate a new feature. The full agent-written essay then follows in a <details><summary> . I use the model name and often the effort level as that summary, to make it abundantly clear what is going on—“Claude Opus 5.5 Medium” for example. My PRs don’t feel nearly as sloppy now! The information is all still there, but a reader can glance at it and get the top, human-curated information without their eyes glazing over at multiple paragraphs of agent-written details. I don’t always write the introduction myself—sometimes the agent has given me what I need already, hidden away in the avalanche of other text. My promise to the reader is that the short opener will represent my human judgement as to what is definitely worth their time. Here are some recent examples where I’ve used this pattern, including the opener I used: I used to have trouble remembering the order of the tags—is it <details><summary> or <summary><details> ? Here are two tricks that helped me. First, and most obviously, the <summary> is clearly the bit where you summarize the details. That’s the tag for your line of text that can be clicked to expand—the <details> element must then wrap everything else. An even better trick is to always refer to these two tags as “details-summary”. “details-summary” is two syllables followed by three syllables. That rolls off the tongue more smoothly than the three-two punch of “summary-details”. Say “details-summary” out loud just a few times and you’ll never forget the order of the tags again. (I still wish GitHub would add a button to their Markdown editor for this—partly to save me painstakingly typing it on my mobile keyboard, and partly to help spread the word to more GitHub users that this feature exists.) This is Hide your slop PR descriptions behind <details><summary> by Simon Willison, posted on 9th November 2026 . title: The U.S. Census Bureau and “Super Intelligence”
abstract: I was reminded today of AI Adoption Rate Trending Down for Large Companies , a chart produced by Apollo Global Management in September 2025, which appeared to show a slowdown in U.S. corporate AI adoption based on numbers collected by the U.S. Census Bureau. At the time I used that chart to demonstrate GPT-5 data analysis , and then to experiment with Claude’s new Code Interpreter . I decided to try running those numbers again to see what had changed over the past year, and in doing so learned that the Bureau has fallen foul of Executive Order 14434 , aka the asinine Super Intelligence one. Every two weeks the U.S. Census Bureau runs a survey called the Business Trends and Outlook Survey (aka BTOS). Each time it goes to 200,000 businesses out of 1.2 million total—the surveyed group (a “panel”) cycles such that an individual business only completes the survey every twelve weeks. The latest data is published on alternating Thursdays at 10am. I used the most recent numbers (published October 22, 2026) to create a new version ( GPT-6 Astra Extra High transcript ) of the AI adoption chart, updated to reflect both the last twelve months and a change that was made to the survey question sent out by the Bureau: Here’s a link to the larger image . For comparison, here’s that AI adoption chart from last year (my GPT-5 version): In September 2025 the largest (250+ employees) companies answered “yes” around 12% of the time to the question about whether they used AI in “producing goods or services”. Under the new “any business function” wording, by February 2026, those same large companies answered “yes” around 30% of the time, and by October 2026 that had increased to around 40%. The data in the above chart comes from the “Employment size class” XLSX file, available from here . Here’s a copy of the file I used. You can view the survey document that is sent out to businesses—here’s my snapshot copy of that 346KB PDF. As the chart demonstrates, the question asked by the Bureau changed in a material way on November 17th, 2025. Prior to that date, the question they asked was this (emphasis mine): In the last two weeks, did this business use Artificial Intelligence (AI) in producing goods or services ? (Examples of AI: machine learning, natural language processing, virtual agents, voice recognition, etc.) On December 3rd, 2025, the Bureau announced a significant change to that question. Here’s the replacement: In the last two weeks, did this business use Artificial Intelligence (AI) in any of its business functions ? (Examples of AI: machine learning, natural language processing, virtual agents, voice recognition, etc.) No more “producing goods or services”—now it’s “in any of its business functions”! This means that the answers to the question before and after November 17th are not directly comparable. When I went looking for the updated question language in the latest XLSX file, I couldn’t find it. I found this instead: In the last two weeks, did this business use Super Intelligence or SI (formerly referred to as Artificial Intelligence or AI) in any of its business functions? (Examples of SI use include: SI-powered data analysis; generative SI for marketing, product design, or coding; virtual SI agents for customer service; SI-powered forecasting or pricing; SI-driven computer vision for quality control, etc.) The BTOS about page explains what happened: Beginning with the October 19, 2026 collection, instrument wording was updated due to Executive Order 14434 . The current numbers reflect the old Artificial Intelligence survey wording—the first survey results reflecting the Super Intelligence wording are due for publication on Thursday. The obvious open question here is whether this wording change is going to affect the survey results. The businesses answering this survey will have last seen that question twelve weeks ago, when it was still called AI. Hopefully the new language isn’t going to confuse them, especially since the survey helpfully spells out “formerly referred to as Artificial Intelligence or AI”. I can’t help but laugh at the absurdity of “SI-powered data analysis; generative SI for marketing, product design, or coding; virtual SI agents for customer service” though. This is The U.S. Census Bureau and “Super Intelligence” by Simon Willison, posted on 2nd November 2026 . title: What Frontier Labs Buy: A Data Deep Dive with Handshake AI — Garrett Lord & Team
abstract: This is our first Latent Space deep dive with an AI data company . In roughly a year, Handshake’s AI training business went from launch to $1 billion in gross annualized revenue . What are frontier labs buying at that scale? What evals are models still nowhere close to human level on? Garrett Lord brought the people who build these reinforcement learning environments to show us. For the first time, we are walking through them live! To cover the scope of Handshake, we had to produce a very special joint podcast across our Science/Engineering/Research/Finance podcast hosts, because Handshake’s business runs across all these and more. Watch for three segments after the general intro: Finance. In the finance demo, the agent has to find its assignment in a bank’s email, work out which files govern the deal, and deliver a workbook. Watch what happens to one line in the client’s email about existing goodwill. The agent carries the number into Python and subtracts it. Collin points out that the model can explain the tax treatment when you ask it directly. The mistake comes when it has to recognize that this particular line of code is where the rule applies. Bio. Nick Magazine and Jonas Mueller show us VIALS, Handshake’s benchmark for interpreting the images scientists use at work. Nick puts nine slides of brain-tumor tissue on screen and asks which two show the most advanced vessel necrosis. Give yourself a moment before his answer. Nick picks H and I. The model picks those two and adds G. Watching Nick point to what’s missing from the tissue is more instructive than seeing the score. Coding. In a simulated file-access task, the team can inspect which files an agent read, whether it checked the copies, and what it did to the shell history afterward. A transcript of the agent’s final reply would miss most of what Steve Kelling and Nishant Ranka are evaluating. 🟣 AI data business — Garrett Lord, Sahil Bhaiwala and Nishant Ranka open and close the episode on the market for expert data. 🌸 Life sciences — Nick Magazine and Jonas Mueller put the gel and brain-tissue tasks on screen. 🟢 Finance — Collin Schweiker and Sahil Bhaiwala take us through Project Falcon and its Excel grader. 🟠 Alignment — Steve Kelling and Nishant Ranka follow the agent’s tool calls through the safety simulations. ATLAS-Finance — Explore the benchmark for agents working across a simulated bank’s inboxes, documents, and financial models. Inside a bank — Handshake traces a separate published deal, Project Osprey, from the client’s email to a grading decision. The deal on screen in our interview is Project Falcon. VIALS sample tasks — Try the scientific image questions, including the gel and brain-tissue tasks from the episode. How Handshake trained a model to read scientific figures — The team describes using intermediate image descriptions to train and evaluate a vision-language model. 0:00 Inside Handshake AI 0:39 Garrett, Sahil and Nishant on frontier training data 5:15 How to build a banking environment for an agent 13:07 How frontier labs buy data 15:51 How a lab evaluates a new dataset 20:01 Testing training data on open models 27:38 Where rubrics fall short of expert judgment 31:30 Nick and Jonas introduce the VIALS benchmark 35:52 Reading molecular structures and plasmid maps 43:48 Training vision models to interpret scientific images 47:17 Task one: reading the bands on a gel 50:59 Task two: finding necrosis in brain tissue 55:49 Can Python tools help the model see? 1:02:52 Can biology models improve on their own? 1:06:19 What a biology lab can buy from Handshake 1:12:33 Atlas Finance with Collin and Sahil 1:18:56 Inside a simulated investment bank 1:25:45 Where the agent’s financial model went wrong 1:31:18 How a banker grades the spreadsheet 1:41:12 Penalty traps, dependency gates and partial credit 1:46:41 How an agent gamed the Excel grader 1:48:52 What would make an AI banker useful? 1:54:48 Safety and alignment with Steve and Nishant 1:58:25 CAREBench and the limits of a refusal 2:04:42 How safety feedback reaches model training 2:07:21 When an agent sends the wrong files 2:11:14 A loan application tests fair lending 2:16:09 Designing private benchmarks for enterprises 2:25:37 The leadership team on Handshake’s mission 2:28:36 When enterprises need their own models 2:33:03 The market for compute and expert data 2:39:12 Why labs hold out evaluation tasks 2:43:01 Hiring at Handshake AI

title: How Stanford Teaches AI-Native Engineering — Mihail Eric, Monaco
abstract: The AI Engineer YouTube channel just crossed one million subscribers . Thank you to everyone who’s watched a talk, sent one to a teammate, or put something they learned into production. For this special, we wanted to sit down with someone who has to answer a question a lot of us are asking at work: what should a software engineer actually learn now? Mihail Eric has two places to test his answer. He teaches The Modern Software Developer at Stanford and leads AI at Monaco, where his colleagues use coding agents to ship software and investigate outages. I asked him to take us through the syllabus, then tell us which parts survived contact with his own engineering team. This is also meant as a preview for all of you joining us in San Francisco for AIE Code next week, as required knowledge for all the conversations with the speakers, sponsors and attendees you’re about to have. If you can see this as a LS subscriber and haven’t got a ticket yet, you can use this code for 30% off (no refunds, sorry) The first run of CS146S had nine assignments and a capstone. In one exercise, students ran an AI code reviewer on a repo and evaluated its feedback. By the next run, Mihail figured students could one-shot a lot of those exercises. When he asked a room of Stanford sophomores and juniors how they coded, everyone he surveyed was already using an agent. So this time, part of the homework is contributing to an open-source project. The person who maintains the repo reviews the student’s patch. I like what that does to the assignment. You can ask an agent to implement a feature in an afternoon. You still have to find out whether the maintainer wants it, why the code behaves the way it does, and what else your patch might break. That conversation is also how a junior engineer gets to learn from a senior one. There’s an exercise in the episode you can borrow for your next PR. Geoffrey Litt’s explain-diff skill turns a change into a visual walkthrough, then quizzes you about it. Try it on a patch your agent just wrote. Which question do you have to reopen the code to answer? Watch the discussion . At Monaco, the team evaluated code review products and kept using Devin. Agent workspaces went the other way. A background agent needs somewhere to run the product, reproduce a failure and test the patch. The details depend on how Monaco’s cloud is set up, so the team built its own workspaces. Mihail’s rule of thumb: “You buy to learn, and you build to keep.” One result is Hal. An engineer can ask it to investigate something that broke and open a PR. A salesperson can ask the same system how the product works. In one case the useful answer is a change someone can review. In the other, it’s an explanation you can give a customer. Give both people a wall of debugging output and you’ve only served one of them. The question I kept coming back to was what happens at the other end of the PR. An agent sees the current code. Where does it look to find out why the team rejected this same change six months ago? That takes us from Basis’s Authority Map to Mihail’s prediction that open-source repos will become agent-run software factories. It’s a good reason to send a student to a maintainer today. Someone still has to decide which change belongs in the project. If you’re building with coding agents, come join us at AI Engineer CODE . And if you’ve been teaching this stuff yourself, I’d love to hear which assignment you had to rewrite first. Stanford CS146S — The ten-week syllabus, assignments and open-source partners. You can also switch to the previous year’s course to compare. Build a coding agent and look inside Claude Code — Mihail’s walkthroughs of the tool loop and the harness around it. Understanding is the new bottleneck — Geoffrey Litt’s approach to learning what changed in an AI-written diff. Monaco’s agent-developer workspaces — The team’s reasoning for building a place where agents can run and test the app. How to Kill the Code Review and the underlying Faros study — Teams with high AI adoption merged 98% more PRs, while their PR review time was 91% longer. Basis’s Authority Map — Where an agent should look for current behavior, earlier decisions and intent. Stripe’s Minions — A production example of giving background coding agents an environment and a path to an engineer-reviewed PR. Boris Cherny’s Steps of AI Adoption — The five stages we pull up on screen near the end of the episode. Mihail on The Thinking Mode — EO Studio’s interview, excerpted at the start of ours. 0:00 · One million AI Engineer subscribers and the CODE Summit 0:51 · Mihail Eric and Stanford CS146S 5:26 · What junior engineers need to learn now 10:02 · Open-source maintainers review the students’ code 15:04 · A tour of the ten-week syllabus 24:04 · The loop, tools and harness inside a coding agent 32:18 · Context engineering for a large codebase 38:15 · Skills that make you understand the diff 46:42 · The Monaco.com dispute and the airplane banner 50:23 · What Monaco does for sales teams 59:21 · Inside Monaco’s engineering team 1:01:40 · “You buy to learn, and you build to keep” 1:05:24 · Making repos agent-ready and closing the on-call loop 1:12:37 · When code review becomes the bottleneck 1:20:37 · Security, dependencies and permissions 1:30:13 · Background agents and Stripe’s Minions 1:34:16 · MCP portals and why infrastructure converges 1:41:22 · Building the software factory 1:45:24 · What work is left for developers? 1:52:16 · From personal adoption to team autonomy Download the complete text below. title: [One Million AI Engineer Special] How Stanford Teaches AI-Native Engineering — Mihail Eric, Monaco
abstract: What do you assign when a coding agent can finish last year’s homework in one prompt? In the second run of Stanford’s CS146S, Mihail Eric brought open-source maintainers into the course. Students have to learn an unfamiliar repo, propose a change, and explain the patch to the person who might merge it. We invited Mihail, who teaches The Modern Software Developer at Stanford and leads AI at Monaco, to celebrate one million subscribers on the AI Engineer YouTube channel. He opens up the course syllabus and shows us which lessons survived contact with his own engineering team. Monaco built its agent workspaces, bought its code review tools, and gave an on-call agent access to Datadog and GitHub. We ask how he decides which tools his team needs to own. Watch the full interview and screenshares on YouTube . Stanford CS146S — The ten-week syllabus and assignments. The Emperor Has No Clothes — Mihail builds a coding agent from scratch. Demystifying Claude Code — Mihail traces a real agent harness. Monaco’s agent workspaces — How the team sets up a workspace for each agent. How to Kill the Code Review — Our essay on what happens when code generation outruns review. Basis’s Authority Map — How agents distinguish current behavior from earlier design decisions.
